title: Operating Systems, Kernel vs. User Space
instructions: Answer from the lesson. For short-answer and practical items, equivalent technically correct wording/code earns credit.

questions.prompt: Why does an application use a system call to access protected OS services?

options.text: To request a controlled transition to privileged kernel code

questions.explanation: System calls provide a controlled interface to privileged OS functionality.

questions.prompt: Which task is typically handled by the kernel?

options.text: Scheduling CPU time and enforcing memory protection

questions.explanation: Scheduling and memory protection are core OS responsibilities.

questions.prompt: An app receives “permission denied” when opening a file. Name two layers that may be involved.
questions.expected_answer: The application requests the operation; the kernel/filesystem checks identity and permissions and returns an error if access is denied.
questions.explanation: Tests the boundary between user space and kernel space.

questions.expected_answer: User space limits direct access to privileged hardware and kernel memory, improving isolation.

questions.prompt: Describe the high-level steps when an application opens a file.
questions.expected_answer: The exact path varies by OS/runtime, but the kernel mediates protected file access.
